paragraphs: A model can identify an image correctly while relying on an incorrect rationale. This paper argues that prediction accuracy alone therefore misses an important part of evaluating foundation models. Its target is double-correct prediction: getting the answer right and supporting that answer with valid visual reasons. This makes the evidence behind a prediction part of the learning objective.

The approach has two phases. First, the researchers curate a visual recognition dataset with structured rationales. Second, they introduce an optimization method that uses those rationales to guide how the model separates and locates supporting visual evidence. The abstract states that this evidence-learning process does not require manual annotations.

Experiments and ablations report prediction accuracy improvements of up to 10.1% over state-of-the-art models across the evaluated tasks. They also report improvements of 7.5% in localization and 36.5% in disentanglement. Together, these findings support evaluating both answers and their supporting evidence, while showing that improving rationale correctness can accompany better prediction accuracy.
neurips-2024-beyond-accuracy-ensuring-co.tldr: Structured rationales and evidence-guided training improve both visual predictions and the correctness of their supporting reasons.

paragraphs: Reusing a network’s previously learned weights seems like a natural way to train as more data arrives. Yet this warm start can leave a model less able to learn new information, a problem called loss of plasticity. The paper studies this problem even when the data distribution remains stationary, so changing environments are not required for the failure to appear.

The researchers develop a framework intended to resemble practical neural network training and identify memorization of noise as the primary cause of plasticity loss in their stationary setting. This connects the difficulty of continued learning to what the network has retained from earlier training, including information that does not help it generalize.

Their method, Direction-Aware SHrinking, or DASH, aims to selectively forget memorized noise while preserving learned features. Evaluations on vision tasks show improvements in test accuracy and training efficiency. The result supports targeted forgetting as a way to make reuse of learned weights more effective when training continues on incoming data.
neurips-2024-dash-warm-starting-neural-n.tldr: DASH selectively forgets memorized noise to improve continued training from existing weights under stationary data distributions.

paragraphs: Out-of-distribution detection asks whether an input differs from the data a model was trained to handle. For generative language models, existing approaches often examine uncertainty or distances between internal representations, called embeddings. This paper studies why embedding-based detection becomes difficult in mathematical reasoning, where the output space has a high-density structure.

The authors argue that this same structure creates useful differences in how embeddings shift through latent space. Their proposed TV score measures the volatility of an embedding trajectory. The approach therefore uses variation along a trajectory as its detection signal, drawing on information that a distance measurement alone may fail to capture.

In the reported mathematical reasoning experiments, TV score outperforms all traditional detection algorithms evaluated on the generative language models. The authors also describe extension to other applications with similarly dense output spaces, including multiple-choice questions. The central finding is that tracking changes in representations can improve detection in a setting where conventional embedding distances face particular challenges.
neurips-2024-embedding-trajectory-for-ou.tldr: TV score detects unfamiliar mathematical reasoning inputs by measuring volatility in embedding trajectories.

paragraphs: Transformers require substantial computation, but many of their neurons are inactive for a given input. This activation sparsity creates an opportunity to replace parts of a dense network with mixture-of-experts layers that execute selected groups of computations. The paper investigates how the base model’s sparsity affects the efficiency of this conversion.

D2DMoE combines sparsity regularization with a dynamic expert-selection rule. Regularization makes the original model more suitable for efficient conversion. Dynamic-k selection then adjusts the number of experts executed for each token, reflecting the observation that different inputs activate very different numbers of neurons. The method also extends this strategy to projections in multi-head attention.

The authors develop an implementation that turns reduced computation into measured execution-time improvements. Across common language and vision tasks, the method outperforms existing approaches and reduces inference cost by up to 60% without significantly affecting performance. These findings show the value of coordinating model preparation, token-specific computation, and implementation efficiency when exploiting activation sparsity.
neurips-2024-exploiting-activation-spars.tldr: D2DMoE combines sparsity regularization and per-token expert selection to reduce transformer inference cost by up to 60%.

paragraphs: Searching for molecules with desired properties can be expensive because evaluating each candidate’s reward requires computation. A generator that proposes many candidates is therefore useful only if it makes effective use of those evaluations. This paper focuses on sample efficiency: finding promising molecules while limiting the number of reward-function calls.

The proposed algorithm transfers the behavior of a strong genetic algorithm into a learned generative policy through GFlowNets training. Because this training is off-policy, the policy can learn from the genetic algorithm’s search experience. Domain knowledge explicitly built into that algorithm can consequently inform the learned generator, connecting a specialized search procedure with a reusable generative policy.

The authors report state-of-the-art performance on the official molecular optimization benchmark, with substantial gains over previous methods. They also demonstrate effectiveness in designing inhibitors against SARS-CoV-2 using substantially fewer reward calls. These findings support the approach as a way to improve computational efficiency in molecular optimization, where candidate evaluation is a central expense.
neurips-2024-genetic-guided-gflownets-fo.tldr: A GFlowNet learns from a domain-informed genetic algorithm to optimize molecules with fewer expensive reward evaluations.

paragraphs: Models that combine text with images, audio, video, or other inputs can serve many different purposes. That variety makes their progress difficult to characterize through a single task or score. HEMM introduces a systematic evaluation framework that organizes multimodal capabilities around three dimensions: basic skills, information flow, and real-world use cases.

Basic skills include connecting modalities, aligning fine details, reasoning through multiple steps, and using external knowledge. Information flow describes operations such as querying, translating, editing, and combining multimodal content. Use cases cover application areas including multimedia, healthcare, natural sciences, affective computing, and human-computer interaction. These dimensions provide complementary ways to interpret model performance.

Experiments across 30 tasks identify challenging combinations of skills and applications and examine trends associated with model scale, training data, alignment, and training objectives. The findings highlight difficult multimodal interactions and tasks involving reasoning or external knowledge, alongside benefits from data and model scale and effects of instruction tuning. HEMM thus connects evaluation outcomes to more specific directions for model development.
neurips-2024-hemm-holistic-evaluation-of.tldr: HEMM evaluates multimodal models across 30 tasks organized by underlying skills, information flow, and application domains.

paragraphs: Personalizing a text-to-image model requires adapting it to user-specific data so that it can generate images of a particular subject. On devices with limited resources, the memory required for this training can be a major obstacle. Hollowed Net addresses that memory requirement within a LoRA-based personalization approach.

During fine-tuning, the method temporarily removes some deep layers from the diffusion model’s U-Net, creating a smaller training structure. This directly changes the architecture used during personalization, complementing approaches that focus on reducing training steps or the number of updated parameters. After training, the personalized components can be transferred back into the original U-Net for image generation without additional inference memory overhead.

Quantitative and qualitative analyses show that training memory can fall to levels as low as those needed for inference, while personalization quality is maintained or improved relative to existing methods. The findings indicate that temporarily simplifying the training architecture can make subject-specific adaptation more practical on memory-constrained devices.
neurips-2024-hollowed-net-for-on-device-.tldr: Hollowed Net temporarily removes deep diffusion-model layers during personalization to reduce training memory while preserving or improving quality.

paragraphs: Relightable view synthesis starts with photographs of an object under unknown lighting and seeks images from new viewpoints under a chosen illumination. Existing approaches typically recover separate explanations for geometry, materials, and lighting through inverse rendering. The paper identifies optimization through differentiable Monte Carlo rendering as a brittle and computationally expensive part of that process.

IllumiNeRF uses a two-stage alternative. First, an image diffusion model relights each input photograph, using the target environment lighting and estimated object geometry as guidance. Second, the method reconstructs a Neural Radiance Field from those relit images. That representation can then render new viewpoints under the selected lighting.

This ordering makes image relighting the input to 3D reconstruction, avoiding the usual requirement to explicitly disentangle all the scene components through inverse rendering. The authors report state-of-the-art results on multiple relighting benchmarks. Their findings show that this simpler combination of image generation and 3D reconstruction can be highly competitive for the evaluated relightable view-synthesis tasks.
neurips-2024-illuminerf-3d-relighting-wi.tldr: IllumiNeRF relights photographs with a diffusion model, then reconstructs a NeRF to render new viewpoints under the target lighting.

paragraphs: This paper studies how much labeled data is needed to learn a classifier with multiple possible labels under the PAC framework. A known result connects whether learning is possible to the finiteness of the Daniely-Shalev-Shwartz, or DS, dimension of the concept class. However, knowing that learning is possible still leaves a gap in the optimal sample requirement.

The authors improve the dependence of the sample-complexity bound on the target error, reducing the remaining gap to a single logarithmic factor. This narrows uncertainty about how the amount of training data must grow as the desired error becomes smaller. It is a theoretical improvement in learning guarantees.

The paper also formulates two open questions that could yield further progress. One concerns learning with bounded-size lists of candidate labels; the other concerns a new shifting operation for multiclass concept classes. The authors prove that a positive answer to either would settle optimal sample complexity up to logarithmic factors in DS dimension. These are conditional routes forward, not completed resolutions.
neurips-2024-improved-sample-complexity-.tldr: The paper tightens multiclass PAC sample-complexity bounds and identifies two open questions whose positive resolution would close further gaps.

paragraphs: Deploying vision models under different resource budgets calls for networks of different sizes. Learngene approaches address their initialization by extracting a compact module from a large trained model and transforming it into starting weights for smaller or differently sized networks. Existing transformations are manually designed and limited to changes in depth.

LeTs makes this transformation learnable and extends it across both width and depth. An auxiliary model jointly trains the compact module and a set of transformation matrices. To initialize a target network, the method selects parameters from those trained matrices according to its size, using strategies including continuous selection and magnitude-wise selection.

On ImageNet-1K, the authors report that destination networks initialized with LeTs outperform networks trained from scratch for 100 epochs after only one epoch of tuning. On downstream classification tasks, they report better results and surpassing from-scratch training after about 10 epochs within a 300-epoch schedule. These findings show how reusable initialization can substantially reduce the training needed for differently sized models.
neurips-2024-initializing-variable-sized.tldr: LeTs learns width and depth transformations of a compact module to initialize differently sized vision transformers efficiently.

paragraphs: Language models communicate confidence through numbers, wording, tone, and supporting detail. LACIE aims to make that communicated confidence better match answer correctness by explicitly considering how a listener interprets a response. Its objective includes whether the listener will accept an answer, alongside whether the answer is right.

The method generates training data through a speaker-listener game in which a simulated listener judges a speaker model’s outputs. It then treats calibration as preference optimization. Fine-tuning three language models produces better calibration on TriviaQA with respect to simulated listeners, and the reported improvements also transfer to human listeners.

In human evaluation, LACIE leads to 47% fewer incorrect answers being accepted while preserving acceptance of correct answers. Training on TriviaQA also improves truthfulness on TruthfulQA. The analysis finds clearer confidence separation between correct and incorrect responses, including more hedging under uncertainty and more abstention on likely errors. That increased abstention trades recall for precision: the model answers less broadly while becoming more selective.
neurips-2024-lacie-listener-aware-finetu.tldr: LACIE trains language models around listener acceptance, helping people reject incorrect answers while retaining acceptance of correct ones.

paragraphs: This paper explores an agent that learns mathematics by proposing its own conjectures and searching for proofs. Its starting point is a mathematical domain expressed through axioms in dependent type theory. The goal is a self-improving cycle in which the agent generates problems that are challenging enough to teach it something but remain provable.

Constrained decoding and type-directed synthesis ensure that sampled conjectures are well formed, even when the language model begins with random initialization. This construction guarantees valid form, rather than automatically guaranteeing that every conjecture is true. The same model supplies a policy and value function that guide proof search as its ability develops.

The authors also introduce hindsight relabeling methods for proof-search trees to improve sample efficiency in both conjecturing and proving. Experiments in propositional logic, arithmetic, and group theory show that the agent can bootstrap from the axioms alone. Across those domains, it improves at producing true, challenging conjectures and finding proofs, supporting an approach where the learning problems evolve with the learner.
neurips-2024-learning-formal-mathematics.tldr: An agent learns to generate conjectures and prove theorems through a self-improving process that starts from mathematical axioms.

paragraphs: Symmetry-aware networks share weights so that their responses follow known transformations of the input. This can improve generalization and data efficiency, but conventional methods require the relevant symmetry group to be specified beforehand. Fixed symmetry constraints can also restrict architecture choices when the data only partly follows the assumed structure.

This paper learns the weight-sharing scheme itself. It introduces learnable doubly stochastic matrices that act as soft permutations of a canonical weight tensor. These matrices define kernel transformations and are optimized jointly with the downstream task. Regular group representations fit within this construction as a special case, while softer transformations give the model additional flexibility.

The authors show that when a dataset has strong symmetries, the learned permutation matrices converge to regular group representations and the resulting networks effectively become regular group convolutions. They also report that the flexibility allows the method to capture partial symmetries. The contribution is a way to discover useful transformation structure while learning the task, with exact group-like behavior arising under the stated strong-symmetry setting.
neurips-2024-learning-symmetries-via-wei.tldr: Learnable soft permutations let networks discover weight-sharing symmetries, including partial symmetries, during task training.

paragraphs: Learning directly from 3D points becomes difficult to scale as scenes grow larger. LinNet revisits point-based network design with the aim of improving both representation quality and computational efficiency. Its architecture relies on a simple multilayer perceptron, without adding attention or sparse convolution to achieve the reported results.

The first component is disassembled set abstraction, which aggregates local information by handling spatial anisotropy and channel anisotropy separately. The second maps 3D points onto one-dimensional space-filling curves. This ordering enables GPU-parallel downsampling and neighborhood queries with linear complexity, addressing operations that matter when processing large point clouds.

LinNet outperforms most previous methods across the reported indoor and outdoor settings. It achieves mean intersection-over-union scores of 73.7% on S3DIS Area5, 81.4% on NuScenes, and 69.1% on SemanticKITTI validation benchmarks, while running almost ten times faster than PointNeXt. These results indicate that improvements in local aggregation and point organization can make relatively simple point-based networks strong contenders for large-scale 3D representation learning.
neurips-2024-linnet-linear-network-for-e.tldr: LinNet combines efficient local aggregation with space-filling-curve point ordering to improve large-scale 3D learning speed and accuracy.

paragraphs: This paper analyzes learning polynomial targets whose outputs depend only on a low-dimensional projection of the input. Although an input can have many coordinates, the target function uses information from a smaller subspace. The analysis assumes standard Gaussian inputs and studies two-layer neural networks trained with stochastic gradient descent through their mean-field flow.

The authors establish a necessary condition for learnability that depends on both the target function and the expressive capabilities of the activation function. This connects successful learning to a relationship between what must be represented and what the network’s nonlinear components can express. The condition is therefore about the learning problem and model together.

They also prove a closely related sufficient result: a slightly stronger condition guarantees that the loss functional decays exponentially to zero. The necessary condition itself is not claimed to be sufficient. By placing these two conditions close together, the work narrows the gap between identifying obstacles to learning and guaranteeing convergence within the stated Gaussian-input, subspace-sparse polynomial setting.
neurips-2024-mean-field-analysis-for-lea.tldr: A mean-field analysis gives closely related necessary and sufficient conditions for learning subspace-sparse polynomials under Gaussian inputs.

paragraphs: Offline statistical estimation works with data generated under a fixed design, while online estimation must handle adaptively chosen covariates. This paper asks whether an offline estimator can be reused as a black box to solve the online problem. Its Oracle-Efficient Online Estimation framework restricts the learner to information supplied by successive offline estimators operating on the data stream.

From an information-theoretic perspective, the answer is encouraging. The authors establish algorithms with near-optimal online estimation error and provide a nearly tight characterization of minimax rates within the framework. This shows that indirect access through offline estimators can retain much of the statistical power needed for online estimation.

Computational efficiency creates a separate boundary: those guarantees cannot generally be achieved efficiently. For conditional density estimation, however, the authors obtain a sharper result. Efficient black-box conversion is possible whenever efficient online estimation is possible with unrestricted algorithms. They also apply the theory to interactive decision making, connecting estimation guarantees to algorithms that learn while choosing actions.
neurips-2024-online-estimation-via-offli.tldr: Black-box offline estimators can support near-optimal online estimation statistically, with computational efficiency depending on the estimation problem.

paragraphs: Self-supervised heterogeneous graph learning builds representations from graphs without relying on task labels for its learning signal. The paper identifies two weaknesses in existing methods: message passing can introduce structural noise into node representations, and learning can make insufficient use of information about clusters. Both can weaken performance on later tasks.

The authors revisit the problem through spectral clustering and propose a framework with rank constraints and two forms of consistency. A rank-constrained clustering method refines the affinity matrix, which represents relationships between nodes, to remove noise. Node-level and cluster-level consistency constraints then capture both invariant information and the broader grouping structure.

The theoretical analysis shows that the learned representations form distinct partitions according to the number of classes and have improved generalization across tasks. Experiments report substantial gains over existing methods on several downstream tasks. Together, the results support treating noise reduction and cluster structure as connected parts of representation learning, rather than relying only on information propagated between neighboring nodes.
neurips-2024-revisiting-self-supervised-.tldr: A spectral-clustering framework improves heterogeneous graph representations through affinity refinement and node- and cluster-level consistency.

paragraphs: Combining convolution and attention at fine image resolution can duplicate expensive processing. GLMix gives the two operations different levels of detail to work with. Convolutions extract local features on a regular image grid, while multi-head self-attention models global relationships among a much smaller collection of semantic slots.

Each layer connects these representations through differentiable soft clustering and dispatching modules. Clustering links fine-grained image features to the coarse slot representation, and dispatching enables information exchange back to the grid. This lets local detail and global information interact while concentrating attention computation on a compact representation.

Across the evaluated vision tasks, attention over a small number of slots, such as 64, is sufficient to match recent state-of-the-art backbones with greater efficiency. Visualizations also show meaningful semantic grouping learned using only ImageNet-1K classification supervision. The authors suggest that this grouping may improve interpretability and inspire weakly supervised segmentation approaches; those possibilities are distinct from the demonstrated backbone performance.
neurips-2024-revisiting-the-integration-.tldr: GLMix combines fine-grid convolutions with attention over coarse semantic slots to improve vision-backbone efficiency.

paragraphs: Selecting a useful subset of training data can make fine-tuning more efficient, but the selection criterion matters. This paper’s generalization analysis extends variance-minimization ideas to high-dimensional fine-tuning. It identifies an additional concern: reducing the problem to a low-rank approximation can introduce bias, so good selection must account for both sources of error.

Sketchy Moment Matching addresses them in two stages. Gradient sketching first explores the fine-tuning parameter space to identify an informative low-dimensional subspace and control approximation bias. Moment matching then selects data to reduce variance within that subspace by matching statistical properties of the selected and original datasets.

The authors prove that gradient sketching is fast and accurate, and that selecting n samples through variance reduction in the subspace preserves a generalization rate of O(dim(S)/n), independent of the full parameter dimension. Synthetic experiments illustrate the bias-variance balance, while vision fine-tuning experiments demonstrate the method’s effectiveness. The contribution links scalable subset selection to a theoretically motivated choice of which parameter directions to preserve.
neurips-2024-sketchy-moment-matching-tow.tldr: Sketchy Moment Matching selects fine-tuning data by controlling approximation bias and matching moments in an informative low-dimensional gradient subspace.

paragraphs: A vision model may need to operate under resource limits that change over time. Scala addresses this by training one vision transformer to contain multiple usable subnetworks of different widths. Its starting observation is that narrower vision transformers can be represented as subnetworks within a wider one, providing a natural way to vary inference size.

During training, Scala activates several subnetworks. Isolated Activation separates the smallest subnetwork from the others, while Scale Coordination supplies each subnetwork with learning objectives intended to be simpler, steadier, and accurate. These mechanisms support training multiple widths together without changing the original vision transformer structure.

Across different evaluated tasks, a single training run produces slimmable representations that match the performance of separately trained networks. Relative to prior work, Scala reports an average improvement of 1.6% on ImageNet-1K while using fewer parameters. The findings indicate that flexible inference capacity can be learned jointly, allowing a trained network to offer multiple operating sizes as available resources change.
neurips-2024-slicing-vision-transformer-.tldr: Scala trains one vision transformer with multiple usable widths, enabling inference that adapts to changing resource budgets.

paragraphs: Diffusion models can restore detailed images, but super-resolution methods face a tension between image quality and inference cost. Some do not fully use large pretrained models, while others require many forward passes beginning from random noise. DoSSR aims to retain pretrained generative capabilities while making the restoration process substantially faster.

The method begins its diffusion process with the low-resolution image. A domain shift equation connects this starting point with existing diffusion models, providing a way to use their learned image prior. The authors then turn the discrete shifting process into a continuous formulation called DoS-SDEs, which supports customized fast sampling solvers.

On synthetic and real-world datasets, DoSSR reports state-of-the-art performance with only five sampling steps. It also achieves a five- to seven-fold speedup relative to previous diffusion-prior-based methods. These findings suggest that changing the starting point and mathematical sampling process together can improve efficiency while preserving the benefits of a powerful pretrained model in the evaluated super-resolution settings.
neurips-2024-taming-diffusion-prior-for-.tldr: DoSSR starts diffusion from low-resolution images and uses domain-shift solvers to achieve strong super-resolution results in five sampling steps.

paragraphs: Temporal sentence grounding locates the part of a video that matches a written query. Traditional formulations assume that a matching segment exists, which can lead to an erroneous result when the requested content is absent. This paper introduces a task that explicitly includes both possibilities: locate relevant content when present, and report its absence otherwise.

The proposed RaTSG network treats this as a foreground-background detection problem, checking for query-related meaning at both frame and whole-video levels. A relevance discriminator combines information at multiple granularities to assess whether the video matches the query. A relation-aware grounding module then selectively performs localization according to the presence or absence of relevant segments.

The researchers reconstruct two established temporal-grounding datasets to create a benchmark for this expanded task. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of RaTSG in that setting. The contribution changes both the evaluation problem and the model behavior, making the decision that a video contains no relevant segment an explicit part of video retrieval.
neurips-2024-temporal-sentence-grounding.tldr: RaTSG locates video segments matching a query and provides relevance feedback when the requested content is absent.

paragraphs: Bayesian optimization searches for good inputs to expensive, noisy functions. When the function changes over time, the optimizer must continually track a moving optimum. Old observations can lose relevance, arbitrary input-time pairs cannot be queried freely, and the algorithm needs to collect fresh observations quickly enough to follow the changes.

W-DBO addresses this by deciding which observations remain useful for future predictions. Its criterion uses Wasserstein distance to quantify relevance, and the algorithm removes observations judged irrelevant as optimization proceeds. Dataset maintenance becomes part of the optimization method, supporting both predictive performance and a high sampling frequency.

The approach also handles continuous-time optimization with an unknown horizon, where the duration of the tracking problem is not specified in advance. Numerical experiments show W-DBO outperforming state-of-the-art methods by a substantial margin. The results support selective removal of stale observations as a practical way to balance the value of historical data against the need to respond to a changing objective.
neurips-2024-this-too-shall-pass-removin.tldr: W-DBO uses a Wasserstein-distance relevance criterion to discard stale observations while tracking changing optimization targets.

paragraphs: Models deployed on small devices may encounter changing data and need to adapt during use. Test-time adaptation offers one route, but conventional approaches can exceed device memory through full backpropagation or large update batches. Limited support for normalization layers on microcontrollers creates another obstacle to bringing these methods onto constrained hardware.

TinyTTA combines a self-ensemble with a batch-agnostic early-exit strategy. This enables adaptation with small batches, reduces memory use, and improves latency while handling distribution shifts. The work also introduces the TinyTTA Engine, a microcontroller library designed to support adaptation directly on the device.

Experiments on a Raspberry Pi Zero 2W and an STM32H747 microcontroller report accuracy improvements of up to 57.6%, memory reductions of up to six times, and faster, more energy-efficient adaptation. In the reported comparison, TinyTTA is the only framework able to perform test-time adaptation on the STM32H747 under a 512 KB memory constraint while maintaining high performance. The results connect algorithm design with demonstrated execution on constrained hardware.
neurips-2024-tinytta-efficient-test-time.tldr: TinyTTA uses early-exit self-ensembles to make test-time adaptation feasible on devices with severely limited memory.

paragraphs: Few-shot semantic segmentation uses a small amount of labeled support information to identify corresponding regions in a query image. This paper investigates how a pretrained latent diffusion model can support that task. Its motivation is that diffusion models learn useful visual structure from unlabeled data, including capabilities relevant to semantic correspondence and segmentation.

The resulting framework, DiffewS, focuses first on interaction between the query and support images. It introduces key-value fusion within self-attention to connect their information. The authors also examine how to incorporate the support mask and how the query mask should provide supervision, addressing both the examples supplied to the model and the signal used to train it.

DiffewS preserves much of the original latent diffusion model’s generative framework so it can make effective use of pretrained knowledge. Experiments show substantial improvements over previous state-of-the-art models in multiple settings. The work presents this few-shot framework as a foundation for future diffusion-based generalist segmentation models, while its demonstrated results concern the evaluated segmentation settings.
neurips-2024-unleashing-the-potential-of.tldr: DiffewS adapts pretrained latent diffusion models for few-shot segmentation through query-support attention fusion and mask-informed learning.
